Insurer-appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the impugned award dated 30.04.2018 awarded by Upper Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sarangarh, District- Raigarh (C.G.) in Claim Case No. 20/2016, whereby the Tribunal allowed the application filed under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 in part, calculated total compensation of Rs. 30,29,632/- on account of death of the deceased Venudhar Sidar in this claim petition.
2.

entities.text: Upper Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sarangarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case in nutshell is that on 27.04.2016 at about 9:00 am the deceased Venudhar along with his friend Haldhar Yadav was going to Government High School, Village- Bar where he was a peon on his Motor Cycle bearing registration no. CG 13 UH 3450.

when they reached near Village- Jampali,
one white colored pick up bearing registration no. OD 17 G 0328 coming from Baramkela hit the motorcycle from front causing severe injuries to the deceased.

When the injured Venudhar was taken to the government hospital Baramkela he was declared dead by the doctor after which a crime has been registered against the driver Ravi Shankar Bariha by Police Station Sariya under Sections 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.

3. Respondent No. 1 to 5 have filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 seeking total compensation of Rs. 55,97,000/- pleading therein that on the date of accident, deceased was peon in Government High School, Village- Bar thereby earning Rs. 13,000/- per month.

4. Respondent No. 6 and 7 have submitted their written statement in which they have stated that at the time of the incident the driver of the offending vehicle was having an effective and valid license.
Therefore, they should not be liable for any amount of compensation and the application should be rejected against them.

Even after that if any liability arises out of the said accident then it should be solely fastened upon Respondent No. 3 because at the time of incident the vehicle was insured with Respondent No. 3.
5.

Appellant/insurance company of the offending vehicle presented his written statement and states that Respondent No. 6 (driver of the offending vehicle) was not having a valid license at the time of the incident, hence if any damages arises out of the accident, Appellant is not responsible for the fulfillment on the basis of this ground alone.
Also, the deceased was driving his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner because of which the said incident happened.

Thus, the deceased is solely The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Jyotsna Sidar on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174412875/
2 responsible for his act.

sentences.text: Therefore, appellant has pleaded to cancel the application forthwith.

6. Upon appreciation of pleadings and evidence placed on record by respective parties, Tribunal held that Venudhar/deceased died on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver/Respondent No. 6 due to which he suffered grievous injuries and as a consequence he died.

Accordingly, Tribunal allowed application in part and awarded Rs. 30,29,632/- with interest @ 6%
per annum, fastened liability upon the appellant and respondent No. 6 and 7.
7.
Learned Counsel for Respondent No. 1 to 5 stated that the award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and needs no interference.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties at length, considered their rival submissions and perused the records with utmost circumspection.

9. So far as the breach of insurance policy is concerned, I have perused the record with utmost circumspection and found that as per Ex. D/4, the driver Ravi Shankar Bariha S/o Vasudev Bariha possesses a driving license for MCWG, LMV (NT) which was valid from 16.11.2015 to 15.11.2035.
The Insurance Company did not produced any evidence of RTO to rebut the same.
Therefore, the learned Trial Court has rightly concluded that there is no fundamental breach of policy.

10. So far as the contributory negligence is concerned, the claimants have examined A.W.-02,
Chandramani Yadav who deposed in his deposition that the accident occurred on 27.04.2016.

The deceased Venudhar was going from Village Chavaripali to High School, Bar where he was working as peon on his motorcycle with son-in-law of Tarpali then suddenly a white colored Pick up came from the direction of Baramkela and the driver of the said pick up dashed the motorcycle of the deceased by driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
In his cross-examination, he deposed that he was going from his village Barpali to Village Chevaripali at around 10:30 am.
He has admitted that there was head on collision of the offending vehicle pick up and the motorcycle.

He further denied that the pick up was being driven by the driver on the middle of the road instead he admitted that the pick up was being driven on the left side of the road and the head on collision of the pick up and the motorcycle occurred.

11. Considering the statement of eye witness A.W.-2, Chandramani Yadav in para 4 of his deposition,
this Court has found that the accident took place due to a head on collision between the vehicle pickup bearing No. OD 17 G 0328 driven by Respondent No. 6 and the motorcycle bearing no. CG 13 UH 3450 driven by the deceased.
On the date of the accident, Respondent No. 6 was driving on the left side and the deceased had gone to the left side while driving the motorcycle.
From this it is clear that there was a contributory negligence of the deceased.
Hence looking to the deposition of the eye witness and finding of the Trial Court, this Court finds that deduction of 30% is appropriate in regard to contributory negligence.

12. Learned Claims Tribunal has awarded :
 S.No. Particulars Awarded by the Court  1.

Monthly income of the Rs. 12,896/-

After deducting 30% of the awarded amount towards contributory negligence, the Respondent No. 1 to 5 would be entitled to Rs.
